correction: My statement that superseding necessarily changes the predecessor attempt identity was specific to the round-one whole-object identity implementation. It is not a contract requirement. A validated stable identity over an immutable attempt header is compatible with the approved design.
test_contract: Require the identified supersession proof to bind the exact predecessor attempt identity, predecessor effect identity or null, prior observation identity, current observation identity and exact changed_fields.
Preserve the predecessor's observed result bytes, transition identity and result identity unchanged.
Require reciprocal predecessor/successor relationships and validate their separately identified link or chain representation.
Retain the prior effect during successor preparation/execution; after successor success, keep the prior effect recoverable through retained history and the supersession proof.
Create reidentified records with broken reciprocal links, proof identities, observation bindings or effect-history bindings and require deterministic rejection.
representation_rule: Tests must not prescribe whether attempt.identity covers the whole mutable envelope or a stable immutable header. Stable-header identity is expressly allowed when disposition, reciprocal links, transition chain and effect history have their own validated identities and the complete relationship is checked.
